source: A Living Rivalry Engine - Examples, Possibilities, and Guidence.md

paths.name: The Unexpected Nemesis
paths.group: Paths created by the player's actions
paths.text: You defeat a seemingly ordinary trainer. They take the loss personally, study your team, and begin preparing specifically for you.

paths.name: The Accidental Hero
paths.group: Paths created by the player's actions
paths.text: You save their Pokémon, help them through an event, or intervene in a crisis. They become inspired by you—or resent needing your help.

paths.name: The Stolen Spotlight
paths.group: Paths created by the player's actions
paths.text: You receive recognition, a sponsorship, a rare Pokémon, or a tournament invitation they expected to earn.

paths.name: The Merciful Victor
paths.group: Paths created by the player's actions
paths.text: You defeat them but spare their pride, offer advice, or help their injured Pokémon. They may become grateful, obsessed with repaying you, or frustrated by your pity.

paths.name: The Public Humiliation
paths.group: Paths created by the player's actions
paths.text: A battle goes badly for them in front of spectators. They may seek revenge, reinvent their style, or withdraw from competition.

paths.name: The Shared Disaster
paths.group: Paths created by the player's actions
paths.text: You both survive a disastrous route, raid, or powerful encounter. You become connected through a shared experience.

paths.name: The Pokémon's Choice
paths.group: Paths created by the player's actions
paths.text: A Pokémon bonds with you, rejects their training, or repeatedly reacts to your presence. The trainer's response creates the rivalry.

paths.name: The Rival You Inspired
paths.group: Paths created by the player's actions
paths.text: They begin by copying your team or strategy, then gradually develop a style of their own.

paths.name: The Rival You Neglected
paths.group: Paths created by the player's actions
paths.text: You repeatedly defeat or encounter them without acknowledging them. They interpret your indifference in a way that drives their next decisions.

paths.name: The Debt
paths.group: Paths created by the player's actions
paths.text: You owe them a favor, they owe you one, or a past decision leaves an unresolved obligation that resurfaces later.

paths.name: The Self-Made Challenger
paths.group: Paths created by the rival's own ambitions
paths.text: They independently decide that you are the best benchmark for their progress.

paths.name: The Chosen Successor
paths.group: Paths created by the rival's own ambitions
paths.text: A respected trainer, Gym Leader, or Champion identifies both of you as potential successors, creating an unspoken competition.

paths.name: The Family Legacy
paths.group: Paths created by the rival's own ambitions
paths.text: They come from a famous battling family and see your success as either a threat to their inheritance or a chance to prove themselves.

paths.name: The Fallen Prodigy
paths.group: Paths created by the rival's own ambitions
paths.text: Once considered exceptional, they are now struggling to recover their former ability.

paths.name: The Late Bloomer
paths.group: Paths created by the rival's own ambitions
paths.text: They begin with an unimpressive team but develop unusually strong bonds and steadily improve.

paths.name: The Researcher
paths.group: Paths created by the rival's own ambitions
paths.text: They study Pokémon behavior, battle data, Hyper surges, or Overdrive events. You become their most fascinating case study.

paths.name: The Collector's Rival
paths.group: Paths created by the rival's own ambitions
paths.text: They pursue rare Pokémon, unusual forms, or remarkable team combinations. They compete with you for discoveries rather than badges alone.

paths.name: The Regional Idealist
paths.group: Paths created by the rival's own ambitions
paths.text: They believe the region needs a particular kind of Champion and decide you represent the opposing future.

paths.name: The Disgraced Champion Candidate
paths.group: Paths created by the rival's own ambitions
paths.text: They once stood on the verge of greatness before a public failure, scandal, or devastating loss.

paths.name: The World Traveler
paths.group: Paths created by the rival's own ambitions
paths.text: They have their own journey across regions and may return with new partners, strategies, and attitudes.

paths.name: The Assigned Opponent
paths.group: Paths created by circumstances and other characters
paths.text: A mentor, tournament, academy, or organization pairs you together. The rivalry becomes genuine—or the arrangement falls apart.

paths.name: The Mutual Enemy
paths.group: Paths created by circumstances and other characters
paths.text: You both oppose the same dangerous trainer or faction but disagree over how to handle it.

paths.name: The Former Friend
paths.group: Paths created by circumstances and other characters
paths.text: A friendship deteriorates because of ambition, conflicting ideals, a betrayal, or a misunderstanding.

paths.name: The Rival's Rival
paths.group: Paths created by circumstances and other characters
paths.text: You defeat someone they have spent years trying to surpass, inheriting that person's attention.

paths.name: The Pokémon League Prospect
paths.group: Paths created by circumstances and other characters
paths.text: A league organization tracks both of you as promising competitors, turning ordinary encounters into a growing public competition.

paths.name: The Shared Mentor
paths.group: Paths created by circumstances and other characters
paths.text: You train under the same expert. Different lessons and interpretations create a philosophical rivalry.

paths.name: The Ideological Opponent
paths.group: Paths created by circumstances and other characters
paths.text: They believe your approach to training, evolution, Hyper, or Overdrive is fundamentally wrong.

paths.name: The Accidental Competitor
paths.group: Paths created by circumstances and other characters
paths.text: You keep meeting at contests, routes, raids, or events. Neither initially cares, until the pattern becomes personal.

paths.name: The Inherited Conflict
paths.group: Paths created by circumstances and other characters
paths.text: A rival believes your actions, family history, team legacy, or previous trainer's reputation wronged them.

paths.name: The Pokémon Who Remembers
paths.group: Paths created by circumstances and other characters
paths.text: One of their Pokémon recognizes you from an earlier encounter, a rescue, a battle, or a period when it belonged to someone else.

personalities.name: The Perfectionist
personalities.text: Repeats training routines and punishes their own mistakes. Strong consistency; risks overtraining and rigidity.

personalities.name: The Prodigy
personalities.text: Learns quickly and expects natural excellence. Powerful early, but may struggle after a humiliating loss.

personalities.name: The Underdog
personalities.text: Believes effort can overcome almost any disadvantage. Adapts well under pressure, but may take unnecessary risks.

personalities.name: The Tactician
personalities.text: Studies team composition, move interactions, and opponent habits. Strong counterplay; can be slow to improvise.

personalities.name: The Gambler
personalities.text: Prefers high-risk, high-reward battles. Can create spectacular victories and spectacular collapses.

personalities.name: The Showboat
personalities.text: Wants an audience and memorable victories. Thrives in public battles but can be distracted by humiliation or applause.

personalities.name: The Veteran
personalities.text: Values preparation and reliable fundamentals. Excellent resource management; can underestimate unconventional opponents.

personalities.name: The Speedrunner
personalities.text: Wants to progress as efficiently as possible. Builds streamlined teams and dislikes delays, detours, or prolonged battles.

personalities.name: The Golden Retriever
personalities.text: Enthusiastic, supportive, and genuinely happy to battle. Bonds quickly and often inspires team confidence.

personalities.name: The Gentle Giant
personalities.text: Calm, patient, and protective. Excels at steady trust-building and defensive coordination.

personalities.name: The Tease
personalities.text: Uses humor and playful provocation. Tests whether opponents lose composure; may hide genuine insecurity.

personalities.name: The Ice Queen/King
personalities.text: Emotionally reserved and difficult to read. Relies on routine and may struggle to express affection directly.

personalities.name: The Social Climber
personalities.text: Pursues status, powerful connections, and public recognition. May abandon a path that no longer improves their reputation.

personalities.name: The Loner
personalities.text: Trains independently and avoids asking for help. Can develop highly individualistic team chemistry, but trust takes time.

personalities.name: The Mediator
personalities.text: Resolves conflict among people and Pokémon. Keeps a balanced team but may avoid difficult confrontations.

personalities.name: The People-Pleaser
personalities.text: Wants everyone to be proud of them. Can develop excellent bonds, yet struggles with boundaries and independent decisions.

personalities.name: The Idealist
personalities.text: Believes every Pokémon deserves dignity and a chance. Resists exploitative strategies, even at a competitive cost.

personalities.name: The Pragmatist
personalities.text: Believes good intentions are meaningless without results. Makes efficient choices and questions sentimentality.

personalities.name: The Traditionalist
personalities.text: Respects established training methods and regional customs. Gains stability from routines but may resist new approaches.

personalities.name: The Innovator
personalities.text: Experiments with strange teams, unconventional moves, and unusual bond-building methods. Can discover unique tactics.

personalities.name: The Naturalist
personalities.text: Studies Pokémon in their environments and adapts to their instincts. Develops species-specific synergies.

personalities.name: The Scholar
personalities.text: Seeks to understand the mechanics behind power. Excels at observing Hyper and Overdrive behavior.

personalities.name: The Spiritualist
personalities.text: Treats battling as a relationship between trainer and Pokémon, not merely a competition. Strong emotional alignment, but may interpret setbacks too personally.

personalities.name: The Nihilist
personalities.text: Believes victory is temporary and bonds are fragile. May fight with cold efficiency until an event challenges that worldview.

personalities.name: The Perpetual Runner-Up
personalities.text: Always comes close to winning, then loses at the critical moment. May learn composure or become consumed by comparison.

personalities.name: The Burnout
personalities.text: Once loved battling but now struggles to care. Small acts of kindness or a surprising defeat can rekindle their motivation.

personalities.name: The Obsessive
personalities.text: Focuses almost entirely on one goal or one opponent. Develops specialized counters but neglects other relationships.

personalities.name: The Avenger
personalities.text: Connects competition with an unresolved wrong. Strong persistence; may mistake revenge for progress.

personalities.name: The Control Freak
personalities.text: Wants every action to be predictable. Trains through rigid commands and struggles when Pokémon act independently.

personalities.name: The Escapist
personalities.text: Uses travel and battling to avoid a personal problem. Their arc can involve facing the issue rather than winning more battles.

personalities.name: The Self-Saboteur
personalities.text: Retreats or makes reckless choices when success becomes possible. Their growth depends on accepting that they deserve to succeed.

personalities.name: The Fallen Idealist
personalities.text: Once believed deeply in fair play but has become cynical after betrayal or repeated disappointments.

personalities.name: The Collector
personalities.text: Values discovery, unusual species, and variety. Rotates their team often and may struggle to develop deep synergy with every partner.

personalities.name: The Natural Talent
personalities.text: Seems casual and effortless, but has an unseen history of practice. Can frustrate rivals who believe effort should be visible.

personalities.name: The Caretaker
personalities.text: Prioritizes Pokémon health and happiness. Avoids unnecessary risks and may withdraw from a battle when a partner is genuinely overwhelmed.

personalities.name: The Chaos Agent
personalities.text: Enjoys disrupting expectations. Uses unpredictable tactics and constantly changes routines.

personalities.name: The Secret Softie
personalities.text: Acts intimidating or dismissive in public but is deeply affectionate in private. Their Pokémon may reveal the truth before they do.

personalities.name: The Reluctant Battler
personalities.text: Battles for practical reasons rather than personal ambition. Their motivation can grow through friendships, discoveries, or protecting someone.

personalities.name: The Former Antagonist
personalities.text: Starts with questionable methods but has the capacity to change. Their actions, not a single apology, determine whether others trust them.

personalities.name: The Quiet Observer
personalities.text: Says little but notices everything. Builds accurate opponent profiles and may be one of the most dangerous late-game rivals.

styles.name: Blitz
styles.text: Applies early pressure and attempts to end battles quickly.

styles.name: Snowball
styles.text: Builds momentum after each knockout or successful setup.

styles.name: Glass Cannon
styles.text: Uses powerful attacks and accepts defensive vulnerability.

styles.name: Executioner
styles.text: Preserves resources until an opponent is weakened, then commits decisively.

styles.name: Combo Artist
styles.text: Chains move effects, status, abilities, and team roles into planned sequences.

styles.name: Berserker
styles.text: Becomes more aggressive as the battle deteriorates, especially after a partner falls.

styles.name: Revenge Striker
styles.text: Builds plans around punishing the Pokémon that defeated a previous partner.

styles.name: Overdrive Specialist
styles.text: Constructs the team around creating, exploiting, and surviving Overdrive windows.

styles.name: Fortress
styles.text: Prioritizes durability, recovery, and safe switching.

styles.name: Attrition
styles.text: Wins by draining resources and forcing repeated unfavorable decisions.

styles.name: Trapper
styles.text: Limits switching and punishes predictable patterns.

styles.name: Counterpuncher
styles.text: Absorbs pressure and retaliates when the opponent overcommits.

styles.name: Stallbreaker
styles.text: Specializes in dismantling defensive teams and recovery loops.

styles.name: Guardian
styles.text: Protects key team members and uses defensive support to preserve its ace.

styles.name: Disruptor
styles.text: Uses status, stat changes, move denial, and confusion to undermine plans.

styles.name: Sacrificial Strategist
styles.text: Willingly trades one team member's position to secure a larger advantage—unless that conflicts with their bond philosophy.

styles.name: Scout
styles.text: Uses early turns to learn about the opponent before committing.

styles.name: Counter-Builder
styles.text: Changes its team or moves between encounters based on remembered battles.

styles.name: Gambit
styles.text: Sets up a specific high-risk tactical payoff.

styles.name: Improviser
styles.text: Abandons planned sequences quickly when circumstances change.

styles.name: Mirror Match
styles.text: Copies the opponent's broad strategy to prove superiority or expose weaknesses.

styles.name: Anti-Meta
styles.text: Builds specifically to punish the most common strategies in the region.

styles.name: Resource Manager
styles.text: Carefully budgets healing, consumables, switches, and once-per-battle mechanics.

styles.name: Specialist
styles.text: Focuses on a type, weather, terrain, or a narrow tactical identity.

styles.name: Conductor
styles.text: Coordinates multiple Pokémon around complementary roles and carefully timed switches.

styles.name: Protector
styles.text: Prioritizes keeping one partner safe, even if it costs a tactical advantage.

styles.name: Trust Fighter
styles.text: Uses risky team plays that depend on strong bond-based synergy.

styles.name: Instinctive Duo
styles.text: Favors improvisational combinations that reflect a trainer and Pokémon's shared habits.

styles.name: Ace-Centric
styles.text: Builds the team to support one signature Pokémon.

styles.name: Rotating Ensemble
styles.text: Treats the entire team as a cooperative unit, with no single permanent star.

styles.name: Bond Breaker
styles.text: Tries to disrupt the opponent's trust, confidence, or team rhythm rather than merely dealing damage.

styles.name: Last Stand
styles.text: Saves resources for a dramatic late-game comeback and a possible Hyper/Overdrive climax.

offscreenEvents.name: Shared Meal
offscreenEvents.text: The trainer learns a Pokémon's food preferences. Affection rises; future scenes may reference a favorite treat.

offscreenEvents.name: Camp Routine
offscreenEvents.text: The Pokémon develops a preferred spot or activity during rest. Repeated routines can create a recognizable habit.

offscreenEvents.name: Grooming and Care
offscreenEvents.text: The trainer helps maintain the Pokémon's comfort and appearance. Trust may rise, especially for a nervous Pokémon.

offscreenEvents.name: Play Session
offscreenEvents.text: A playful Pokémon becomes more confident; a reserved one may slowly begin initiating interactions.

offscreenEvents.name: Quiet Companionship
offscreenEvents.text: The Pokémon chooses to sit near the trainer without prompting. A small but meaningful signal of growing trust.

offscreenEvents.name: Preferred Sleeping Arrangement
offscreenEvents.text: A Pokémon begins sleeping closer to its trainer or another team member. This can reveal attachment or a need for reassurance.

offscreenEvents.name: Greeting Ritual
offscreenEvents.text: The pair develops a unique greeting, gesture, or routine that may appear in later scenes.

offscreenEvents.name: Comfort After a Bad Day
offscreenEvents.text: The Pokémon comforts a distressed trainer, reversing the usual caretaker dynamic and potentially changing the trainer's motivation.

offscreenEvents.name: Technique Practice
offscreenEvents.text: The trainer and Pokémon repeat a specific technique. Success depends on aptitude, condition, instruction quality, and time invested.

offscreenEvents.name: Failed Drill
offscreenEvents.text: Repeated failure can produce frustration, adaptation, or a decision to try another teaching method.

offscreenEvents.name: Independent Practice
offscreenEvents.text: A Pokémon trains on its own initiative. High-autonomy Pokémon may develop faster when allowed to experiment.

offscreenEvents.name: Friendly Sparring
offscreenEvents.text: Team members practice against one another, improving coordination but potentially creating a competitive rivalry.

offscreenEvents.name: Tactical Review
offscreenEvents.text: The trainer reviews a previous battle and identifies a mistake. The next encounter may show the correction.

offscreenEvents.name: Move Experimentation
offscreenEvents.text: The trainer tries a new move combination or tactical role. It may work, fail, or become a signature technique after repeated use.

offscreenEvents.name: Adaptive Exercise
offscreenEvents.text: The trainer changes a drill to accommodate the Pokémon's personality or limitations. This can build trust and improve learning efficiency.

offscreenEvents.name: Overtraining Incident
offscreenEvents.text: A trainer pushes too far, producing short-term progress and a longer recovery requirement.

offscreenEvents.name: Recovery Day
offscreenEvents.text: The trainer deliberately rests a Pokémon. Proper recovery can improve readiness and reduce strain.

offscreenEvents.name: Hyper Control Practice
offscreenEvents.text: The Pokémon learns to enter or exit Hyper more reliably, if that is supported by the existing mechanics.

offscreenEvents.name: Technique Breakthrough
offscreenEvents.text: A difficult move, combination, or control method finally clicks after a history of practice.

offscreenEvents.name: Fearful Refusal
offscreenEvents.text: A Pokémon hesitates to perform a dangerous action. The trainer can respect the hesitation, encourage it carefully, or react badly.

offscreenEvents.name: Unwanted Separation
offscreenEvents.text: A Pokémon becomes separated from the group during exploration. Reuniting them can produce relief, fear, or a new protective habit.

offscreenEvents.name: Jealousy
offscreenEvents.text: A Pokémon reacts to a trainer giving another partner more attention. The cause may be insecurity, competitiveness, or a genuine change in routine.

offscreenEvents.name: Unexpected Attachment
offscreenEvents.text: A Pokémon bonds with an unlikely teammate, changing team cohesion or creating tension with another partner.

offscreenEvents.name: Conflict Over Tactics
offscreenEvents.text: The Pokémon resists a battle plan that conflicts with its instincts or preferences. The trainer must adapt or insist.

offscreenEvents.name: Apology
offscreenEvents.text: The trainer acknowledges a mistake after a difficult encounter. The result depends on whether their later behavior supports the apology.

offscreenEvents.name: Earned Independence
offscreenEvents.text: The trainer lets a Pokémon make a major decision. This may improve autonomy and synchronization.

offscreenEvents.name: A Broken Promise
offscreenEvents.text: The trainer fails to follow through on a promise. Trust may decline, especially if the promise was repeated or deeply meaningful.

offscreenEvents.name: The Protective Intervention
offscreenEvents.text: A Pokémon intervenes to protect a partner despite being told to stay back. The event may reveal loyalty, impulsiveness, or a developing bond.

offscreenEvents.name: The Unspoken Reconciliation
offscreenEvents.text: Two partners resume a familiar activity after a period of tension. The relationship improves subtly without an explicit conversation.

offscreenEvents.name: Wild Pokémon Encounter
offscreenEvents.text: A Pokémon interacts with wild members of its species. This can affect confidence, curiosity, or the trainer's understanding of its needs.

offscreenEvents.name: Rescue Operation
offscreenEvents.text: The team helps a wild Pokémon or another trainer. The event can shape the rival's values and create future allies.

offscreenEvents.name: Team Member Missing
offscreenEvents.text: A Pokémon leaves the immediate group for a believable reason, prompting the trainer to reflect on how it has been treated.

offscreenEvents.name: Shared Environmental Challenge
offscreenEvents.text: The team crosses a difficult environment together. The event may strengthen teamwork or expose a weakness.

offscreenEvents.name: Another Trainer's Advice
offscreenEvents.text: A mentor, rival, or stranger offers advice. The trainer may accept it, reject it, or misunderstand it.

offscreenEvents.name: Public Praise
offscreenEvents.text: A Pokémon receives recognition for a performance. This can build confidence or create pressure to keep impressing others.

offscreenEvents.name: Public Embarrassment
offscreenEvents.text: A failed performance is witnessed by others. The Pokémon and trainer may respond very differently to the same event.

offscreenEvents.name: Raid Cooperation
offscreenEvents.text: A rival's Pokémon works with unfamiliar Pokémon during a raid, potentially developing a new tactical preference or bond.

offscreenEvents.name: Hyper/Overdrive Witness Event
offscreenEvents.text: A rival witnesses another Pokémon's breakthrough and reconsiders their own training philosophy.

offscreenEvents.name: Unexpected Act of Compassion
offscreenEvents.text: A trainer chooses to help a struggling opponent or Pokémon despite a competing goal. The action can change how their own team sees them.

arcs.name: The Prodigy Learns Humility
arcs.text: Expects to win naturally. | Learns to respect preparation, collaboration, and opponents.

arcs.name: The Underdog Finds Their Method
arcs.text: Tries to copy stronger trainers. | Develops a style that fits their own strengths.

arcs.name: The Perfectionist Accepts Failure
arcs.text: Treats every mistake as unacceptable. | Learns to adapt rather than endlessly repeat the same routine.

arcs.name: The Loner Learns to Trust
arcs.text: Avoids help and emotional attachment. | Builds a reliable support network without losing independence.

arcs.name: The Showboat Finds Meaning
arcs.text: Cares about recognition. | Learns to value the relationship behind the performance.

arcs.name: The Burnout Rediscovers Joy
arcs.text: Battles out of obligation. | Finds a new reason to compete—or chooses a different life.

arcs.name: The Reluctant Champion
arcs.text: Doesn't want the responsibilities of success. | Decides what kind of Champion they actually want to become.

arcs.name: The Late Bloomer Emerges
arcs.text: Is dismissed as unremarkable. | Achieves success through patience and self-knowledge.

arcs.name: The Copycat Becomes Original
arcs.text: Copies the player's team and techniques. | Develops an independent identity and may surpass their inspiration.

arcs.name: The Obsession Spiral
arcs.text: Defines success around beating one opponent. | Learns to pursue personal goals—or becomes consumed by obsession.

arcs.name: The Fall from Grace
arcs.text: Loses status after a major defeat. | Rebuilds honestly or resorts to desperate shortcuts.

arcs.name: The Champion's Shadow
arcs.text: Lives under a famous predecessor's reputation. | Establishes their own legacy or remains trapped in comparison.

arcs.name: The Broken Promise
arcs.text: A betrayal damages a central relationship. | Reconciliation, permanent separation, or a new understanding.

arcs.name: The Power at Any Cost
arcs.text: Pursues Hyper/Overdrive without sufficient control. | Learns restraint or suffers increasingly serious setbacks.

arcs.name: The Fear of Winning
arcs.text: Self-sabotages when success becomes possible. | Confronts the insecurity driving the behavior.

arcs.name: The Rival Who Cheats
arcs.text: Justifies unfair tactics to keep up. | Takes responsibility, hides the truth, or doubles down.

arcs.name: The Cold Strategist
arcs.text: Treats Pokémon as interchangeable tools. | Learns to respect individual needs—or embraces an increasingly ruthless approach.

arcs.name: The Fallen Idealist
arcs.text: Loses faith after witnessing unfairness. | Rebuilds their principles or decides that winning matters more than fairness.

arcs.name: The Neglected Ace
arcs.text: A powerful Pokémon receives little care outside battle. | The trainer changes their behavior, the Pokémon withdraws, or the relationship is restructured.

arcs.name: The Pokémon Who Outgrows Its Trainer
arcs.text: A partner becomes more capable and independent. | The trainer adapts, resents the change, or learns to become a better partner.

arcs.name: The Team Divided
arcs.text: Two Pokémon compete for attention or status. | The trainer restores balance or allows the conflict to deepen.

arcs.name: The Fearful Partner
arcs.text: A Pokémon struggles with a particular battle situation. | Gradual confidence, continued accommodation, or a difficult separation from that role.

arcs.name: The Overprotective Trainer
arcs.text: Refuses to let Pokémon take reasonable risks. | Learns to trust their judgment—or remains unable to accept uncertainty.

arcs.name: The Unlikely Pair
arcs.text: Trainer and Pokémon have contrasting personalities. | They find complementary roles or discover that affection cannot solve every incompatibility.

arcs.name: The Partner Who Stayed
arcs.text: A Pokémon remains loyal through repeated hardship. | The trainer finally recognizes the sacrifices that loyalty involved.

arcs.name: The Independent Ace
arcs.text: A Pokémon increasingly acts on its own instincts. | The pair develops mutual trust or becomes unable to work together.

arcs.name: The Shared Recovery
arcs.text: Trainer and Pokémon both struggle after a crisis. | They rebuild together, potentially unlocking a distinctive controlled Hyper/Overdrive expression.

arcs.name: Friends Become Rivals
arcs.text: A supportive relationship turns competitive. | Healthy competition, resentment, or reconciliation.

arcs.name: Rivals Become Friends
arcs.text: Mutual hostility gradually softens. | Cooperation, friendship, or an alliance that remains competitive.

arcs.name: The Rival's Rival
arcs.text: Another trainer competes for the same person, goal, or title. | A three-way rivalry, alliance, or change in priorities.

arcs.name: The Mentor's Disappointment
arcs.text: A respected mentor loses faith in the rival. | Earned reconciliation or independence from the mentor's expectations.

arcs.name: The Regional Reformer
arcs.text: Wants to change how the League operates. | Wins institutional influence, compromises their ideals, or becomes disillusioned.

arcs.name: The Unlikely Protector
arcs.text: Initially prioritizes personal ambition. | Takes responsibility for another trainer, community, or team.

arcs.name: The Rival Who Leaves
arcs.text: Abandons the current competition. | Returns with a different philosophy or never comes back.

arcs.name: The Rival Who Surpasses You
arcs.text: Gradually becomes stronger and more independent. | Forces the player to respond, accepts a new relationship, or moves on.

arcs.name: The Unfinished Rivalry
arcs.text: A major conflict is never properly resolved. | Reopens later, possibly in another region or during a world event.

arcs.name: The Uncontrolled Prodigy
arcs.text: enormous potential, insufficient control. Their progress depends on discipline and honest feedback.

arcs.name: The Trainer Who Feared Overdrive
arcs.text: avoids the mechanic after witnessing a frightening incident. Their arc may involve careful reintroduction or a principled refusal to use it.

arcs.name: The Pokémon Who Refuses
arcs.text: a Pokémon stops cooperating with a trainer's attempts to force a power breakthrough. The trainer must address the relationship, not grind a hidden meter.

arcs.name: The Perfect Synchronization
arcs.text: a pair with exceptional trust develops precise control, but must learn how to cope when one partner's condition changes.

arcs.name: The Artificial Shortcut
arcs.text: a trainer pursues an external shortcut to power. The story can explore unstable results, ethical compromises, or the eventual rejection of the shortcut.

arcs.name: The Overdrive Addict
arcs.text: a trainer becomes obsessed with spectacular power surges, ignoring ordinary fundamentals and the welfare of their team.

arcs.name: The Late Awakening
arcs.text: a seemingly ordinary Pokémon discovers an unusual expression after years of accumulated experience.

arcs.name: The Pokémon Who Saves the Trainer
arcs.text: a crisis reveals that the Pokémon's motivation is protecting its trainer rather than winning.

arcs.name: The Broken Synchronization
arcs.text: a major betrayal damages a previously reliable pairing. The duo must rebuild trust or accept that their old style no longer works.

arcs.name: The Power Without a Bond
arcs.text: a rival can trigger an impressive state through exceptional skill or an unusual mechanism, but struggles with its consistency, meaning, or consequences.

mechanics.name: The Independent Rivalry
mechanics.text: Rivals develop relationships with one another without involving the player. Two rivals may become bitter enemies, close friends, or training partners.

mechanics.name: Rival-to-Rival Pokémon Influence
mechanics.text: A rival's Pokémon can learn from an encounter with another rival's Pokémon. This can affect confidence, battle preferences, and future interactions.

mechanics.name: The Unseen Defeat
mechanics.text: A rival loses off-screen to a trainer who isn't the player. Their response affects their confidence, strategy, and ambitions.

mechanics.name: The Unseen Victory
mechanics.text: A rival wins a major battle and becomes more ambitious. They might rise in regional rankings or attract a sponsor.

mechanics.name: The Training Exchange
mechanics.text: Two rivals exchange training methods, producing new strategies or a shift in their philosophies.

mechanics.name: The Rivalry Triangle
mechanics.text: Three rivals compete for different reasons. Defeating one may help another, but not necessarily improve your relationship with either.

mechanics.name: The Shared Rival
mechanics.text: Multiple characters identify the player as their most important opponent. Each has a different interpretation of what defeating the player would prove.

mechanics.name: The Rival Alliance
mechanics.text: Rivals temporarily cooperate against a common threat, then resume competing when the threat passes.

mechanics.name: The Mentor Network
mechanics.text: A rival seeks advice from a Gym Leader, Champion, researcher, or another rival. Mentors can influence their style and worldview.

mechanics.name: The Signature Technique
mechanics.text: Repeated use of a particular combination may lead a rival to develop a recognizable tactical signature.

mechanics.name: The Team Identity Shift
mechanics.text: A rival changes their roster to reflect a new philosophy, emotional state, or strategic problem.

mechanics.name: The Pokémon Transfer
mechanics.text: A rival may trade, release, or rehome a Pokémon for a story-grounded reason, depending on the game's rules. Such decisions should have real consequences.

mechanics.name: The Return Encounter
mechanics.text: A rival reappears after a long absence with evidence of independent progress, not simply a level increase.

mechanics.name: The Public Reputation System
mechanics.text: Other trainers react to the rival's known victories, losses, sportsmanship, and treatment of Pokémon.

mechanics.name: The Rivalry Rumor Mill
mechanics.text: The player hears partial reports about rivals. Some are accurate; others are incomplete or distorted.

mechanics.name: The Conflicting Account
mechanics.text: Two characters describe the same incident differently, encouraging the player to investigate before making assumptions.

mechanics.name: The Rival's Private Goal
mechanics.text: A rival may pursue a goal that has little to do with defeating the player. The goal can take priority over a battle invitation.

mechanics.name: The Missed Encounter
mechanics.text: If the player fails to meet a rival, the rival still advances their plans. Their next appearance reflects what happened in the meantime.

mechanics.name: The Rivalry Cooldown
mechanics.text: A rival who has repeatedly lost may stop challenging the player temporarily, choosing to recover, retrain, or pursue another goal.

mechanics.name: The Unscheduled Challenge
mechanics.text: A rival may interrupt an appropriate exploration or event with a challenge when the story and gameplay state support it.

mechanics.name: The Challenge Refusal
mechanics.text: A rival can refuse to battle because of injury, a personal commitment, a disagreement, or a belief that the timing is wrong.

mechanics.name: The Rival's Substitute
mechanics.text: If their ace is unavailable, a rival may use a different Pokémon, revealing how well the rest of their team has developed.

mechanics.name: The Legacy Encounter
mechanics.text: A rival remembers a defining earlier battle and deliberately recreates, reverses, or rejects its circumstances.

mechanics.name: The Rivalry Handoff
mechanics.text: An established rival can lose relevance naturally while another character becomes the player's primary competitor.
